items.title: Section: Which Eyes Can See a Particle, and Five Mistaken Ways of Imagining One

items.zh: 問：如是所說五相極微，復有五眼，所謂肉眼、天眼、聖慧眼、法眼、佛眼。當言幾眼用幾極微為所行境？答：當言除肉眼、天眼，所餘眼用一切極微為所行境。何以故？以彼天眼，唯取聚色中表、上下、前後、兩邊、若明、若闇，必不能取極微處所，由極微體以慧分析而建立故。問：何故說極微無生無滅耶？答：由諸聚色最初生時，全分而生；最後滅時，不至極微位，中間盡滅，猶如水滴。復由五相，應知名不如理思議極微。謂於色聚中，有諸極微自性而住，應知名初不如理思議極微。或謂極微有生有滅，或謂極微與餘極微或合或散，或謂眾色於極微量積集而住，或謂極微能生別異眾多色聚，應知名後不如正理思議極微。故應方便以如理思思議極微，斷此五種非理思議。
items.en:
Question: of these five kinds of eye — physical, divine, the wise eye of the noble ones, the dharma eye, and the buddha eye — how many take particles as their object? Answer: excluding the physical and divine eyes, the remaining eyes take all particles as their object.
Question: why is it said the particle neither arises nor ceases? Answer: because when clusters of matter first arise, they arise completely all at once; and when they finally cease, they do not linger down to a particle before ceasing, but cease completely in between — like a drop of water.
There are also five marks by which one should recognise unreasonable ways of conceiving the particle. That particles exist with their own essence within a cluster of matter is the first unreasonable conception. That particles arise and cease, or that particles combine and disperse with one another, or that various forms of matter accumulate and dwell within a fixed particle-quantity, or that particles are able to generate distinct further clusters — these should be known as the remaining unreasonable conceptions. One should therefore make the effort to conceive of the particle reasonably, thereby severing these five unreasonable conceptions.

items.title: Section: Five Benefits of Seeing Through Matter, and the King's Chariot That Could Not Be Found

items.zh: 復次，建立極微，當知有五種勝利。謂由分析一合聚色安立方便，於所緣境便能清淨廣大修習，是初勝利。又能漸斷薩迦耶見，是第二勝利。如能漸斷薩迦耶見，如是亦能漸斷憍慢，是第三勝利。又能漸伏諸煩惱纏，是第四勝利。又能速疾除遣諸相，是第五勝利。如是等類，應當如理思惟極微。
items.en: Furthermore, establishing the particle brings five benefits, one should know. Through the method of analysing a single unified cluster of matter, one is able to cultivate one's meditation object with purity and breadth — this is the first benefit. It further enables the gradual severing of the view of a real self — this is the second benefit. Just as it enables the gradual severing of the view of a real self, so too it enables the gradual severing of pride — this is the third benefit. It further enables the gradual subduing of afflictions generally — this is the fourth benefit. It further enables the swift removal of characteristics — this is the fifth benefit. Things of this kind are how the particle should be reasonably contemplated.

items.title: Section: Five Ways Matter Arises — Beginning With What Derived Matter Depends Upon

items.zh: 復次，略說色物生，當知有五種。何等為五？一、依止生，二、種子生，三、勢引生，四、攝受生，五、損減生。云何依止生？謂於所依大種處所，有餘所造色生，故如是說：由四大種造所造色。是同一處攝持彼義。又若於此色積聚中，有彼大種及所造色自相可得，當知此中即有彼法；若於此處，彼法自相都不可得，當知此處無有彼法，是名總建立有非有相。
items.en:
Furthermore, briefly, matter's arising should be known to be of five kinds: through support, through seed, through generative momentum, through sustaining, and through diminishment. What is arising through support? It is derived matter arising at the very location of the elements it depends upon — hence it is said that the four elements produce derived matter, this meaning that they share one location and sustain it.
Furthermore, if within a given cluster of matter a particular element's and its derived matter's own characteristic can be found, one should know that phenomenon is present there; if that characteristic cannot be found at all, one should know that phenomenon is absent there. This is called establishing presence and absence in general.

items.zh: 若有說言：於此處所，彼法自相雖不可得，然必有者。今應問彼：此不可得與可得者，為物是等？為不等耶？若物等者，物既是等而不可得，不應道理。若不等者，為即此量說物不等？為據威勢說不等耶？若即此量說不等者，少分自相亦不可得，不應道理。若據威勢說不等者，離彼自相有餘威勢不可得故，不應道理。如是等類，當知名依止生。云何種子生？謂所有色，各從自種子所生。如堅硬聚，或時遇緣便生流濕；流濕遇緣復生堅硬。不煗生煗，煗復生冷；不動生動，動生不動。如是好色、惡色等差別應知。由如是等雖無自相，然有其界，從彼彼聚，彼彼色法差別而生。如是等類，當知名種子生。云何勢引生？謂內色根增上力故，外分差別相續而生，謂器世界等。

blocks.text: Why analyse matter into particles at all? The treatise's answer is practical: to clear away the marks the mind clings to.

Not the physical or divine eye. Master Cháng Bǎi: the wisdom eye, dharma eye, and buddha eye know it, through analysis by wisdom. One should not imagine particles combining to form clusters: without arising or ceasing there is no combining. (Untranslated, 0598a07: particles are "without parts": not that they have smaller parts, for a particle is not a cluster; at the particle there is nothing further to divide.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: one can swiftly remove the marks of objects, and attachment goes with them.

Through support, seed, generative momentum, sustaining, and diminishment. Whether an element is present in a cluster depends on whether its own mark can be found there. (Untranslated, 0598b17: an argument against those who say a thing's mark may be unfindable yet the thing still present; then "arising from seed": hard can become fluid and fluid hard, warm cold and still moving, each from its own seeds; and "arising by momentum": the outer world arises through the power of beings' inner faculties.)
The point of analysing a chariot or a body into parts is not physics. It is to loosen the grip of the image we hold.

quiz.q: Which of the five eyes take particles as their object, and why?
options: all but the physical and divine eyes, namely the wise, dharma, and buddha eyes, which have wisdom as their nature
only the physical and divine eyes, since the particle is form and form is seen with an eye faculty
only the buddha eye, and none of the other four
all five, differing only in clarity
quiz.why: The treatise excludes the physical and divine eyes. Master Cháng Bǎi: the wise eye, dharma eye, and buddha eye all have wisdom as their nature, and the particle is known only through analysis by wisdom. So the question turns on the fact that the particle is an object of understanding and not of sight.

quiz.q: Among unreasonable conceptions, why can one not say particles generate clusters of matter?
options: a particle is too small and weak, and only many combined can generate a cluster, one alone being unable to
particles neither arise nor cease, and so neither combine nor disperse; clusters cannot be said to arise from them
clusters are already real and need nothing to generate them
particles generate only mental phenomena, not form
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: without arising or ceasing there is no combining or dispersing, and so one cannot say clusters arise from particles. The first unreasonable view holds that particles have their own nature within clusters, clusters being built of tiny units. The treatise rejects that picture of matter as built up from below, since a cluster arises entire.

quiz.q: The English has "the swift removal of attachment to characteristics" for 除遣諸相. Is what is removed characteristics or attachment?
options: what is removed is attachment, since marks cannot be removed; adding "attachment" is exactly right and fits the literal Chinese
what is removed is form itself, so that form vanishes
what is removed is others' appearance, unrelated to oneself
what is removed is the marks themselves; "attachment" is an addition, the lecture saying object-marks are removed, and with them attachment to phenomena
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: one can swiftly remove the marks of objects, and even attachment to phenomena can be removed. The Chinese object of 除遣 is 諸相, the marks. In meditation the marks themselves are cleared; attachment goes with them. The English "attachment to characteristics" moves the removal from the marks to the attitude, which is an interpretation.

quiz.q: What five kinds of arising of matter does the treatise list?
options: from egg, womb, moisture, transformation, and the intermediate state
from particle, cluster, element, derived form, and absorption's result, arranged from subtle to coarse
through support, through seed, through generative momentum, through sustaining, and through diminishment
of the desire, form, and formless realms, contaminated and uncontaminated
quiz.why: The treatise lists arising through support, seed, generative momentum, sustaining, and diminishment. Master Cháng Bǎi on the last two: what makes a cluster of matter grow is arising through sustaining, and what makes it diminish and fail to grow is arising through diminishment. The treatment of seed arising in the Chinese is missing from the English.

quiz.q: How does the treatise establish presence and absence in general, per Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: every cluster surely has all four elements, even unseen ones, so no test by mark is needed
by whether the eye can see it
by whether the scriptures mention it
one cannot simply say every cluster has all four elements; presence is judged by whether the mark of element or derived form is found
quiz.why: The treatise's criterion: if the own-mark of an element or of derived form can be found in a cluster, that phenomenon is there; if not, it is not. Master Cháng Bǎi: one cannot broadly say every cluster contains all four elements; the distinction turns on whether the own-mark is found. The English "that element is present" narrows 彼法, which also covers derived form.
